newsitem.title: UK: Intertanko to campaign for terminal safety systems.
newsitem.headline: Intertanko to campaign for terminal safety systems.

text.p: Tanker owners are to campaign for improvements to port safety systems and terminal operations in a bid to reduce accidents like last week's oil spill in Japan, Intertanko said on Wednesday.

Intertanko, the international association of independent tanker owners, said it has decided to seek ways to improve port operations following the Diamond Grace oil spill in Tokyo Bay and the Sea Empress grounding off Milford Haven in 1996.
Intertanko managing director Dagfinn Lunde said: "There are clearly deficiencies in the way ports are working round the world."
A meeting of the association's executive committee this week had approved efforts to investigate the issue and campaign for changes, he said.
Chairman of Intertanko, Richard du Moulin, said: "Tanker operations are part of a system depending on accurate charts, pilotage and control of traffic channels."
"The system has not kept pace with improvements to vessels and many ports are deficient," he said
Lunde said Intertanko would sound out the oil majors, most of whom are associate members of Intertanko, in an attempt to agree a joint approach to the issue.
"Owners, authorities and terminals do not co-operate at the moment. It is the charterer who sends a ship to a berth, and it is sometimes only then that the master finds out it is not safe," he said.
"We have to come up with a system to assess terminals, inspect facilities and come up with a database. It is the first time we have had approval to go ahead in this way," Lunde added

Du Moulin said the extreme financial liabilities caused by the Oil Pollution Act of 1990 (OPA90) and the importance of the oil trade in the U.S. meant it was "essential to have a separate focus there."

He added that Intertanko would take up pilotage issues on a global level through the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) and at local levels with groups like the U.S. Coast Guard and the American Pilots' Association.

Intertanko said it was not trying to shift liability on to pilots but it was likely that many problems would be found to be due to human error, and that ultimately terminals might have to put maximum sizes on ships allowed to berth, dependent on the tides. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087.
